knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 3.3.4
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly describes a chi-square goodness-of-fit test, including unknown parameters?
knowledge_checks.body: Select the GOF hypothesis, expected counts, and DF adjustment.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: GOF compares observed counts to expectations under a named distribution. Estimating parameters reduces DF. Independence in a contingency table is a different test.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Test fit to a stated distribution; expected counts from hypothesised probabilities; reduce DF when parameters are estimated.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Equating GOF with independence, or adjusting DF in the wrong direction.

choices.label: GOF tests whether a sample is consistent with a stated distribution. Expected counts come from the hypothesised probabilities and the sample size. If parameters are estimated from the same sample, degrees of freedom are reduced under CMP rules.
GOF is identical to a two-way test of independence; expected counts always use row and column totals only.
When parameters are estimated, degrees of freedom increase by the number of estimated parameters.
Expected frequencies are always set equal to the observed frequencies, so the chi-square statistic is automatically zero.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 3.3.4
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. You test whether claim counts follow a Poisson distribution; λ is estimated from the same sample. Which statement is correct?
knowledge_checks.body: Expected counts and DF adjust; refuse independence-as-GOF.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Fit Poisson probabilities with λ̂, form expected counts, and reduce DF by one for λ̂. Independence testing is not GOF to a named distribution.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: E = n × Poisson probabilities at λ̂; DF = bins − 1 − 1; independence ≠ GOF.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Forgetting the DF reduction for λ̂, or treating independence as GOF.

choices.label: Expected frequencies are n times fitted Poisson probabilities using λ̂. Degrees of freedom are (number of bins − 1 − number of estimated parameters), so subtract 1 for λ̂. A chi-square test of independence in a two-way table is a different procedure.
Expected frequencies use λ̂, but degrees of freedom stay at (bins − 1) with no reduction for estimating λ.
Because λ is estimated, replace GOF by a two-way independence test on a contingency table of counts.
Expected frequencies are n/λ̂ in every bin, regardless of the Poisson probabilities for those bins.
